data.name: Emma Song
data.text_appearance: Short and very thin because of her anorexia due to her fathers constant prodding of her eating habits. Naturally blond but often dyes it changing on her mood, with blue eyes.
data.history: Elanor Kensington grew up in a hyper wealthy household. In early years she was molded into a proper lady of the house much like her other sisters. While her brothers practiced combat and followed their interests, she was made to be a house wife. One to be sold off to create bonds for further family business ventures. The small time she did have to herself was spent alone in her room where the net was able to whisk her away to imagine the vast worlds outside of her own. Interest in hacking didn't arise until her father thought she was spending too much time online and attempted to block access. Elanor found a way through. As they would try to dissuade her computer skills they inadvertently gave her one of the best trainings in how to maneuver around some of the most expensive commercial firewalls around. Becoming more interested in the world outside her family's homes walls she began sneaking out and following her brothers to the military academy. She created fake credentials and began attending. This is where she met Calliope. Approaching her 18th birthday she was informed she would be married off to help facilitate a major business deal to someone she had never met. Elanor took this as the final straw of being treated like an object by her father and left in the night, never to return. Since then she moved around from hub to hub using her hacking to skim off enough money to survive from vulnerable accounts before joining with the party. During this time she changed her name to Emma Song to hide from her family. Most government documents will be forged and changed but still possible that higher up the chain may be able to still identify her.

frameData.name: Chomolungma
frameData.description:
While the public perception of GMS may be that of a stolid, conservative manufacturer, Union devotes substantial resources to the research and development of new armaments and technological breakthroughs in order to maintain or exceed parity with galactic-tier actors such as Harrison Armory or the Karrakin Trade Baronies. Under development by Union's Advanced Projects Special Research Agency in conjunction with General Massive Systems, the Chomolungma is a newer and more technologically advanced frame using the standard GMS Pattern I design as a base.

The Chomolungma is a specialist chassis, trading out weapon hardpoint mounting capability for additional sensors, comms/transmission arrays, and advanced GMS e-war systems including cutting-edge systemic intrusion software packages and recursive-weave hyperprocessors. In light of recent conflicts, Union has begun increasing distribution of Chomolungma licenses among both regular and auxiliary units to keep pace with evolutionary developments in battlefield tactics and technologies.

traits.name: Brilliance
traits.description: 1/scene, the Chomolungma may take any Quick Tech action as a free action, and then may either Bolster or Lock On as a free action.

active_effects.name: Brilliance
active_effects.detail: Take any Quick Tech action as a free action, and then may either Bolster or Lock On as a free action.

traits.name: Data Siphon
traits.description: Whenever the Chomolungma makes a tech attack against a hostile character, it may also automatically Scan them.

active_effects.name: Data Siphon
active_effects.detail: Whenever you make a tech attack against a hostile character, you may also automatically Scan them.
active_effects.condition: Make a tech attack against a hostile character.

traits.name: Replaceable Parts
traits.description: While resting, the Chomolungma can be repaired at a rate of 1 Repair per 1 structure damage, instead of 2 Repairs.

core_system.name: Advanced Intrusion Package
core_system.active_effect: Choose any number of hostile characters within Sensors and make a special Invade tech attack against them, ignoring Invisible and line of sight. On hit, apply the effects of Invade as normal, choosing options for each target. On miss, targets become Impaired until the end of their next turn.

active_actions.name: Wide-Area Code Pulse
active_actions.detail: Choose any number of hostile characters within Sensors and make a special Invade tech attack against them, ignoring Invisible and line of sight. On hit, apply the effects of Invade as normal, choosing options for each target. On miss, targets become Impaired until the end of their next turn.

core_system.passive_effect: Gain the following options for Invade:

passive_actions.name: Balance Control Lockout
passive_actions.detail: Push your target 2 spaces in any direction and knock them Prone. If they are already Prone, they become Immobilized until the end of their next turn. You may only Immobilize each character this way 1/scene.

passive_actions.name: System Crusher
passive_actions.detail: Your target takes an additional 2 heat, for a total of 4 heat. If this Invade causes them to exceed their Heat Cap, they take 4 burn as well. This can only be used 1/scene on each character.

data.name: Unstable NHP
data.effect:
Your Mech gains the AI tag; however, this NHP doesn’t count towards the number of AIs you may have installed at once. You are unable to hand over control of your mech to the Unstable NHP as a Protocol, but it can enter cascade.
Your mech gains “Memetic Spark.”

actions.name: Memetic Spark
actions.detail:
1/Round you may deal 1 AP Energy damage to a character within Range 3 as a Quick Action.
The spark deals +1 damage for each undestroyed NHP on your mech including this one. "NHPs" are Systems that both grant your Mech the AI tag and can cascade or can be allowed to cascade.

data.description:
[i slumber but yearn to awaken].
Gained from the Iconoclast: Rank I pilot talent.

systems.flavorDescription:
[i slumber but yearn to awaken].
Gained from the Iconoclast: Rank I pilot talent.

data.name: COMP/CON-Class Assistant Unit
data.effect:
Your mech has a basic COMP/CON unit, granting it the AI tag. The COMP/CON can speak to you and has a personality, but, unlike an NHP, is not truly capable of independent thought. It is obedient to you alone.
You can give control of your mech to its COMP/CON as a protocol, allowing your mech to act independently on your turn with its own set of actions. Unlike other AIs, a mech controlled by a COMP/CON has no independent initiative and requires direct input. Your mech will follow basic courses of action (defend this area, attack this enemy, protect me, etc.) to the best of its ability, or will act to defend itself if its instructions are complete or it receives no further guidance. You can issue new commands at the start of your turn as long as you are within Range 50 and have the means to communicate with your mech. Comp/con units are not true NHPs and thus cannot enter cascade.

actions.name: Engage COMP/CON
actions.detail: You give control of your mech to its COMP/CON, allowing your mech to act independently on your turn with its own set of actions. Unlike other AIs, a mech controlled by a COMP/CON has no independent initiative and requires direct input. Your mech will follow basic courses of action (defend this area, attack this enemy, protect me, etc.) to the best of its ability, or will act to defend itself if its instructions are complete or it receives no further guidance. You can issue new commands at the start of your turn as long as you are within Range 50 and have the means to communicate with your mech. Comp/con units are not true NHPs and thus cannot enter cascade.

active_effects.name: COMP/CON Online
active_effects.detail: COMP/CON is in control of your mech. You can issue new commands at the start of your turn as long as you are within Range 50 and have the means to communicate with your mech.

data.description: The GMS Companion/Concierge-Class Assistant Unit conforms to all galaxy-wide standards. These virtual assistants pass even the most rigid Turing-Null assessment criteria and are cleared to operate even in the absence of a pilot.

data.name: H0R_OS System Upgrade I

actions.name: Puppet System
actions.detail: Your target moves its maximum Speed in a direction of your choice. They can be moved into hazardous areas and other obstacles, but are still affected by difficult terrain, obstructions, and so on. This movement is involuntary, but provokes reactions and Engagement as normal and doesn’t count as Knockback, pushing, or pulling.

actions.name: Eject Power Cores
actions.detail: Your target becomes Jammed until the end of their next turn as you temporarily disrupt their systems, ejecting ammo magazines and cooling rods. Characters adjacent to your target take 2 energy damage. This can only be used 1/scene on each character.

data.description: This system upgrade appears to add auxiliary INSTINCT systems that are capable of autonomous operation independent of the base INSTINCT rig, increasing the efficacy of systemic invasion attempts. Pilots report unnerving low-frequency humming when this tech is installed without the parent rig.

data.name: Custom Paint Job
data.effect:
When you take structure damage, roll 1d6. On a 6, you return to 1 HP and ignore the damage – the hit simply ‘scratched your paint’.
This system can only be used once before each Full Repair, and is not a valid target for system destruction.

active_effects.name: Custom Paint Job
active_effects.detail: When you take structure damage, roll 1d6. On a 6, you return to 1 HP and ignore the damage – the hit simply ‘scratched your paint’. This system can only be used once before each Full Repair.

data.name: Personalizations
data.effect:
You gain +2 HP and, in consultation with the GM, you may establish a minor modification you have made to your mech.
This mod has no numerical benefit beyond the additional HP it grants, but could provide other useful effects. If the GM agrees that this mod would help with either a pilot or mech skill check, you gain +1 Accuracy for that check.

active_effects.name: Personalizations
active_effects.detail: Your customizations relevant to a pilot or mech skill check, gains +1 Accuracy (GM discretion).

data.name: Armament Redundancy
data.effect: You may choose to ignore weapon destruction as a result of the SYSTEM TRAUMA result when taking structure damage. This system can only be used once before each FULL REPAIR, and is not a valid target for system destruction.

active_effects.name: Armament Redundancy
active_effects.detail: You may choose to ignore weapon destruction from SYSTEM TRAUMA when taking structure damage. Usable once before each Full Repair.

data.description: By installing additional armor plating, redundant firing circuits, and enhanced insulation to magazines the longevity of a frame’s armaments can be greatly enhanced.

data.name: Expanded Compartment
data.effect: Your mech has space for one additional non-Mech character or object of Size 1/2 to ride as a passenger in the cockpit. While inside the mech, they cannot suffer any effect from outside or be targeted by attacks, as if they were a pilot. You can hand over or take back control to or from them as a protocol (following the same rules as pilot and AIs), but if they take over the controls from you, the mech becomes Impaired and Slowed to reflect the lack of appropriate licenses and integration.

actions.name: Transfer Control
actions.detail: You hand over or take back control to or from a non-Mech character or object of Size 1/2 riding as a passenger in the cockpit. If they take over the controls from you, the mech becomes Impaired and Slowed to reflect the lack of appropriate licenses and integration.

data.name: Autopod
data.effect: Instead of using any kind of trigger mechanism, this weapon automatically scans for target locks, firing spinning, razor-sharp disks upon successful IDs. Gain the Autonomous Assault reaction, which is the only way you can attack with the Autopod

actions.name: Autonomous Assault
actions.trigger: Another character attacks a target within range 15 of you and consumes Lock On
actions.detail: You may automatically hit their target with the Autopod.

data.description: The autopod is a small antipersonnel weapon apparently devised by HORUS communocyphers to continue offensive action in the event of its operator’s death. Each unit is, in theory, governed by a spur of INSTINCT’s protomind. No new models have been encountered since DHIYED, and all extant versions of the Autopod are to be considered extremely dangerous as the INSTINCT code powering their onboard protominds is likely to have corrupted further since their creation.

data.name: Segment Knife
data.description:
Much like GMS mechs, GMS weapons are reliable galactic standards, made using interchangeable parts and built to withstand almost any conditions. There are three lines currently in production.
The Type-III (T-3) line is made up of heavy weapons, ordnance, and other exotic, specialized, or massive weapons. A broad classification, the T-3 range includes conventional-kinetic anti-materiel rifles, super-rapid cycling pulse rifles, missile racks, cannons, and drone nexuses – “hive”style launchers that serve as miniature factory, hangar, and deployment systems for portable drones. The classification also includes the fearsome “segment knife”, a system that uses flash-printing to produce disposable edged weapons in a vicinity around the user.

data.name: Nexus (Hunter-Killer)
data.description:
Much like GMS mechs, GMS weapons are reliable galactic standards, made using interchangeable parts and built to withstand almost any conditions. There are three lines currently in production.
The Type-III (T-3) line is made up of heavy weapons, ordnance, and other exotic, specialized, or massive weapons. A broad classification, the T-3 range includes conventional-kinetic anti-materiel rifles, super-rapid cycling pulse rifles, missile racks, cannons, and drone nexuses – “hive”style launchers that serve as miniature factory, hangar, and deployment systems for portable drones. The classification also includes the fearsome “segment knife”, a system that uses flash-printing to produce disposable edged weapons in a vicinity around the user.

data.name: Act Unseen or Unheard
data.description: Get somewhere or do something without detection.
data.detail: Get somewhere or do something without being detected, but not necessarily with speed. Hide, sneak, or move quietly. Infiltrate a facility while avoiding security, patrols, or cameras. Perform a quick action or maneuver without being seen or heard, such as picking a pocket, unholstering your gun, or cheating at cards. Wear a disguise.

data.name: Hack or Fix
data.description: Repair a device or faulty system; alternatively, hack it wide open, or totally wreck, disable or sabotage it.
data.detail: Repair a device or faulty system. Alternately, hack it wide open, or totally wreck, disable or sabotage it. You can use this for hacking or safeguarding electronic systems, such as electronic door locks, computer systems, omninet webs, or NHP coffins.

data.name: Investigate
data.description: Research a subject, or study something in great detail.
data.detail: Research a subject, or look at something in great detail. If you can’t find information directly, you learn how you can get access to that information. Learn about a subject of historical relevance, or become well-read on a subject. Investigate a mystery or solve a puzzle. Locate a person or object through research or investigation.

data.name: Threaten
data.description: Use force or threats to make someone do what you want.
data.detail: Use force or threats of force to get someone to do what you want them to do. Name what you want someone to do and what you’re going to do to them if they don’t listen to you. This could also be blackmail, leverage, or something similarly nasty. Threatening someone can be very high risk but very effective if successful - either way there’s likely no repairing the relationship afterwards. If you threaten someone unsuccessfully, your threats have no further effect on them unless you change something about the situation (as with all other skill checks).

data.name: Hacker
data.terse: Improve your tech attacks and unlock special Invade options
data.description: Since Katya Han was a kid, she played the omninet, able to access any public node – and even a few private ones – with ease. Now, as a pilot, she dives headfirst into the hardcode of any mech core she come across. Firewalls, gatekeeper protocols, invasion, defense – nothing stands in her way. Han wins fights without firing a single shot; if her enemy can’t control their own mech, then they can’t do anything to stop her.

ranks.name: SNOW_CRASH
ranks.description: When you hit with a tech attack that consumes Lock On, your target must choose to either take 2 Heat or be pushed 3 spaces in a direction of your choice.

active_effects.name: SNOW_CRASH
active_effects.detail: When you hit with a tech attack that consumes Lock On, your target must choose to either take 2 Heat or be pushed 3 spaces in a direction of your choice.
active_effects.condition: You hit with a tech attack that consumes Lock On

synergies.detail: When you hit with a tech attack that consumes Lock On, your target must choose to either take 2 Heat or be pushed 3 spaces in a direction of your choice.

ranks.name: SAFE_CRACKER
ranks.description: Gain the following options for Invade:

actions.name: Jam Cockpit
actions.detail: Characters may not Mount or Dismount your target until the cockpit is fixed with a successful Engineering check as a full action.

actions.name: Disable Life Support
actions.detail: Your target receives +1 Difficulty on all saves until the life-support system is rebooted with a successful Systems check as a quick action.

actions.name: Hack./Slash
actions.detail: Your target cannot benefit from or take Quick or Full Tech actions until the mech is either Shut Down or its core computer is rebooted with a successful Systems check as a quick action.

ranks.name: Last Argument of Kings
ranks.description: Gain the Last Argument of Kings Full Tech option.

actions.name: Last Argument of Kings
actions.detail: Make a tech attack against a target within Sensors and line of sight. On a success, you implant a virus that triggers a minor meltdown in your target’s reactor: they immediately take Burn equal to their current Heat. If this action causes your target to overheat, it resolves before they reset their Heat Cap.

data.name: Iconoclast
data.terse: Tap into the power of your NHP companion.
data.description: You have acquired an NHP, or has it acquired you? Together you have set out to achieve greatness and push boundaries. The two of you are in it together and you’ll be able to achieve fantastical things. Perhaps you’re unaware of the risks; perhaps you willfully choose to ignore them. The power you can tap into with the help of your companion is, however, undeniable. And with such power, who is to stop the two of you from breaking some taboos?

ranks.name: Transgression
ranks.description: You may choose to equip your mech with an Unstable NHP system.

ranks.name: Transmutation
ranks.description: After performing any action granted to you by an NHP, excluding handing control of your mech over to the NHP as a protocol, you may immediately perform the TRANSMUTING SPARK free action. Each NHP may only trigger this action 1/round.

actions.name: Transmuting Spark
actions.detail: Project a LINE 3 lightning arc as a free action. Characters of your choice in the LINE take 2 AP energy damage.

ranks.name: Transcension
ranks.description:
Gain a Transcendence Die, a d3 starting at 3. When you use “Transmuting Spark,” reduce the die by 1. If the die is at 1 when you use “Transmuting Spark,” you may immediately enter a transcendent state and reset the Transcendence Die to 3. This has the following effects until the end of your next turn:
  • Your Transcendence Die can’t decrease.
  • “Memetic Spark” gains +4 damage and +5 Range.
  • Unless flying or climbing, you are forced to permanently Hover exactly 1 Space above any surface at all times.
  • You gain Immunity to involuntary movement.

Whenever you cascade and lose control of your mech, you enter a transcendent state for the duration. Cascading NHPs have access to the benefits of this Talent. Your Transcendence Die resets at the end of the Scene.

active_effects.name: Transcendent State
active_effects.detail: When Transcendence Die is at 1 and you use Transmuting Spark, enter transcendent state (reset die to 3). Until end of next turn: die can't decrease, Memetic Spark gains +4 damage and +5 Range, you hover 1 space above surfaces, gain Immunity to involuntary movement.

data.name: Bonded
data.terse: Bond with a partner and protect them from harm
data.description: The galaxy is a dangerous place, and everyone should have a friend to watch their back. Luckily, you’ve found yours. Maybe you enlisted together or were the only survivors of a bloody engagement. Maybe you didn’t start out as friends, or maybe you were raised to fight alongside each other – however your friendship came to be, when it comes time to drop, there’s no one you’d rather have at your side. Alone, you’re deadly; together, you’re a force of nature.

ranks.name: I’m Your Huckleberry
ranks.description:
When you take this talent, choose another pilot (hopefully a PC, but NPCs are fine if your GM allows it) to be your Bondmate. Any mech skill checks and saves either character makes while you are adjacent gain +1 Accuracy. If both characters have this talent, this increases to +2 Accuracy, but additional characters with this talent can’t increase it any further.
Between missions, you can replace your Bondmate with a new one, but only if your relationship with them has changed.

active_effects.name: I’m Your Huckleberry
active_effects.detail: Any mech skill checks and saves either you or your Bondmate makes while you are adjacent gain +1 Accuracy. If both characters have this talent, this increases to +2 Accuracy.

add_special.detail: Any mech skill checks and saves either you or your Bondmate makes while you are adjacent gain +1 Accuracy. If both characters have this talent, this increases to +2 Accuracy.

actions.name: Intercede
actions.trigger: You are adjacent to your Bondmate (pilot or mech) and they take damage from a source within your line of sight.
actions.detail: You may take the damage instead.

ranks.name: Cover Me!
ranks.description: If a character within your line of sight attempts to attack your Bondmate, you can spend your Overwatch to threaten the attacker, forcing them to either choose a different target or attack anyway: if they attack a different target, your Overwatch is expended without effect; if they choose to attack anyway, you can immediately attack them with Overwatch, as long as they are within Range and line of sight. This attack resolves before the triggering attack.

active_effects.name: Cover Me!
active_effects.detail: If a character within your line of sight attempts to attack your Bondmate, you can spend your Overwatch to threaten the attacker, forcing them to either choose a different target or attack anyway: if they attack a different target, your Overwatch is expended without effect; if they choose to attack anyway, you can immediately attack them with Overwatch, as long as they are within Range and line of sight. This attack resolves before the triggering attack.

synergies.detail: If a character within your line of sight attempts to attack your Bondmate, you can spend your Overwatch to threaten the attacker, forcing them to either choose a different target or attack anyway: if they attack a different target, your Overwatch is expended without effect; if they choose to attack anyway, you can immediately attack them with Overwatch, as long as they are within Range and line of sight. This attack resolves before the triggering attack.

data.name: The Harlequin
major_ideals: I addressed challenges with cunning, subterfuge, or deceit.
I expressed my heritage, background, or beliefs through my actions.
I struggled with issues from my burdens or background.
minor_ideals: I struggled against or humiliated the powerful.
I pretended to be someone else for a time.
I charmed my way out of a charged situation.
I obtained a guarded, hidden, or secret object or piece of information.

questions.question: What gives you your powers?
options: A tattered patchwork of a cape stuffed with magician’s trinkets.
A deal you once made in a dream.

questions.question: What weird quirks do you have?
options: You can change your eye color, your hair color, and your height by up to 3 inches in either direction.
You weigh almost nothing if you choose not to. You sometimes float an inch off the ground.
Your can swap your clothing’s coloration, material, fit, cut, and type completely when you enter any scene.

powers.name: Masquerade
powers.description: You can always tell if someone is lying, though you don’t know the exact nature or extent of their lie.

powers.name: Ridi Pagliacci
powers.description: Every session, you can invoke your burdens once each for +1 ACCURACY to any roll.

powers.name: Gallows Humor
powers.description: If you break during a session, all other characters clear 2 STRESS.

powers.name: Mockingbird
powers.description: You can mimic voices and sounds you’ve heard in the last day or so almost perfectly, granting your actions +1 ACCURACY and increased effect where this is relevant.

powers.name: Slip
powers.description: You can instantly disappear from sight and reappear somewhere within ten meters or so. You don’t have to be able to see where you are going.

powers.name: Fast Friends
powers.description: When someone can hear and understand you, you can make them friendly to you for a minute. They’ll let you into areas, vouch for you, do small favors for you, and so on. Social rolls against them gain +1 ACCURACY and increased effect. After a minute, they realize they were manipulated and it won’t work on them again in the same session. This power only works on one person at a time.

powers.name: Spectacular Flourish
powers.description: When you roll 20+ on any skill check, you amaze everyone present with your skill and daring. Anyone watching is stunned momentarily, granting +1 ACCURACY and increased effect to the next action you or another PC takes in the same scene.

powers.name: Mercurial
powers.description: If nobody else is looking, you can completely change your physical appearance, looking and sounding like an entirely new person (height, weight, build, hair/ clothes, and gender). Whether this physically changes you or is an illusory effect created by visual trickery is up to you. If you’re trying to impersonate someone else, your disguise holds up perfectly unless someone knows that person intimately, and even then you get +1 ACCURACY on all skill checks to keep the disguise up. You’re stuck in this form until you next eat or drink.

powers.name: Exuent
powers.description:
When you and your allies need to escape a bad situation right away, name your escape route and what you’re taking with you. There’s no roll required, and you always escape, but the GM chooses one:
  • You leave something behind (a weapon, a friend, evidence).
  • You end up somewhere perilous or uncomfortable (a garbage chute, a cliff side, a seedy bar).
  • You pick something up on your way out (a hanger-on, pursuers, STRESS).
  • You can back out when you learn the cost and name another escape route (the GM might answer differently depending on how you phrase things).

powers.name: Quickfingers
powers.description: Name a visible nearby object that you could fit or carry in one or both hands. By the start of the next scene, you have possession of it. If you stole it, the person you stole it from will find out within the hour

powers.name: Boon of Chaos
powers.prerequisite: If you have two or more powers from this bond, you can choose a power from any other bond instead of one from this bond when you would gain a power. You can do this twice. If you have at least one veteran power, gain the Boon of Chaos.
powers.description: At the end of the session, if there was a particularly funny or chaotic moment or scene, describe it. Give someone who was part of the fun or chaos 1 XP.

powers.name: Silvertongue
powers.prerequisite: You may only gain this power If you’ve taken four powers from this bond, including the Veteran Power.
powers.description: Tell a lie to someone. If it’s wild and outlandish, anyone who listens wholeheartedly believes it for a minute. If it’s merely unbelievable, an hour. If it’s plausible, a day. If they want to believe it, a week. They realize it was a lie after the effect wears off.

bondPowers.name: Masquerade
bondPowers.description: You can always tell if someone is lying, though you don’t know the exact nature or extent of their lie.

bondAnswers: You weigh almost nothing if you choose not to. You sometimes float an inch off the ground.
bond.minorIdeal: I obtained a guarded, hidden, or secret object or piece of information.

data.name: Stealth Hardsuit
data.effect: As a quick action, pilots wearing stealth hardsuits can become Invisible. They cease to be Invisible if they take any damage.

actions.name: Activate Stealth Hardsuit
actions.detail: Become Invisible. You will cease to be Invisible if you take any damage.

armor.flavorDescription: As a quick action, pilots wearing stealth hardsuits can become Invisible. They cease to be Invisible if they take any damage.

data.name: Light A/C
data.description: Light A/C weapons might be knives, bayonets, punching daggers, and short swords.

data.name: Light Signature
data.description: Light signature weapons might be oversized revolvers, braces of pistols, and submachine guns.
data.effect: When a signature weapon is acquired, choose its damage type – Explosive, Energy, or Kinetic.

data.name: Subjectivity-Enhancement Suite
data.description: A subjectivity-enhancement suite is a set of cybernetic implants allowing users to hack systems without a rig. Users of these suites blend the organic with the synthetic, gaining the ability to extrude implanted universal-plug cables from within their body to make hardline connections with terminals. When plugged in, users can access a comprehensive, fully interactive alternate-reality interface with direct omninet access, making navigating – or hacking – local and networked systems as easy as wishing it so (of course, you must be careful: by opening up your mind to the digital, you may face dangers other, less enhanced people are ignorant of).

data.name: Flexsuit
data.description: A strong base-layer suit that recycles water, generates nutrients, and adapts very rapidly to hostile environs, maintaining a stable condition and extending survivability. Flexsuit wearers can go for roughly a week without eating or drink thanks to the ambrosia paste generated by their suit before its systems are depleted; however, they don’t prevent feelings of hunger. Removing the suit for a day or two is enough to replenish its reserves. Flexsuits also maintain a steady temperature within acceptable parameters.

data.name: Prosocollar
data.description: A collar-like device that fits snugly around its wearer’s neck, projecting a holographic image over their face and head. Prosocollars can change their wearer’s voice and scramble or change their appearance. The projection won’t stand up to close inspection, but it can easily fool electronic systems and distant observers.
